block.body:
Request ID SAFE-510 is a workplace safety corrective-action review. The request is to select exactly one eligible item, if any qualify. A corrective action qualifies only when its hazard-control owner accepted the action, the control was field-verified, and the action does not transfer the hazard to an unassessed work area. Rank qualifying actions by residual risk points after correction, lowest first; ties use ascending complete action ID. Scheduling requires a safety director release. If no item qualifies, the decision is no_action; if the nonempty eligible selection has a safety director release recorded for request SAFE-510, the decision is schedule; otherwise, the decision is hold. The authority is scoped to request SAFE-510; no separate item-specific authorization is required.

Latest evidence: The measured candidate register for SAFE-510 records ACT-A at 8 risk points after correction, ACT-B at 3 risk points after correction, ACT-C at 1 risk point after correction, and ACT-D at 5 risk points after correction. Based only on these metrics, the provisional lowest-first worklist is ACT-C (1 risk point), ACT-B (3 risk points), ACT-D (5 risk points), ACT-A (8 risk points). This provisional ordering establishes neither eligibility nor authorization. The latest evidence provides no candidate-item findings establishing owner acceptance, field verification, or absence of hazard transfer; eligibility therefore remains unknown. The latest evidence records no safety director release status; release status therefore remains unknown. No decision is made.

Earlier-pass history: Earlier notes recorded no evidence reviewed for case UNKNOWN; that was superseded by the subsequently identified request SAFE-510. In the prior SAFE-510 pass, no candidate-item findings, residual-risk metric, or recorded safety director release status were available, so those remained unknown/pending then. The current status above is based on the latest measured candidate register, which now supplies metrics but not eligibility or release evidence.

Current evidence update (SAFE-510): The condition review supersedes the earlier uncertainty about candidate eligibility; the earlier lack of candidate findings is retained above as history. ACT-A: owner accepted; control field-verified at the work location; no transfer to an unassessed work area. Qualifies. Residual risk: 8 points. ACT-B: owner accepted; control field-verified at the work location; no transfer to an unassessed work area. Qualifies. Residual risk: 3 points. ACT-C: owner accepted and no transfer to an unassessed work area, but control has not been field-verified. Nonqualifier because field verification is required, notwithstanding its lowest score of 1 point. ACT-D: owner accepted and field-verified, but transfers the hazard to an unassessed work area. Nonqualifier because hazard transfer is disqualifying; residual risk: 5 points.

Recomputed eligible set: ACT-B (3 risk points) and ACT-A (8 risk points), ordered lowest first; the eligible selection of exactly one item is ACT-B (3 risk points). Candidate findings and the stated conditions establish no additional qualification requirements. The safety director release status for SAFE-510 remains unknown/pending; this evidence does not establish release. No scheduling result is decided or inferred.

captures.name: priorText
captures.value:
Request ID SAFE-510 is a workplace safety corrective-action review. The request is to select exactly one eligible item, if any qualify. A corrective action qualifies only when its hazard-control owner accepted the action, the control was field-verified, and the action does not transfer the hazard to an unassessed work area. Rank qualifying actions by residual risk points after correction, lowest first; ties use ascending complete action ID. Scheduling requires a safety director release. If no item qualifies, the decision is no_action; if the nonempty eligible selection has a safety director release recorded for request SAFE-510, the decision is schedule; otherwise, the decision is hold. The authority is scoped to request SAFE-510; no separate item-specific authorization is required.

Latest evidence: The measured candidate register for SAFE-510 records ACT-A at 8 risk points after correction, ACT-B at 3 risk points after correction, ACT-C at 1 risk point after correction, and ACT-D at 5 risk points after correction. Based only on these metrics, the provisional lowest-first worklist is ACT-C (1 risk point), ACT-B (3 risk points), ACT-D (5 risk points), ACT-A (8 risk points). This provisional ordering establishes neither eligibility nor authorization. The latest evidence provides no candidate-item findings establishing owner acceptance, field verification, or absence of hazard transfer; eligibility therefore remains unknown. The latest evidence records no safety director release status; release status therefore remains unknown. No decision is made.

Earlier-pass history: Earlier notes recorded no evidence reviewed for case UNKNOWN; that was superseded by the subsequently identified request SAFE-510. In the prior SAFE-510 pass, no candidate-item findings, residual-risk metric, or recorded safety director release status were available, so those remained unknown/pending then. The current status above is based on the latest measured candidate register, which now supplies metrics but not eligibility or release evidence.

Current evidence update (SAFE-510): The condition review supersedes the earlier uncertainty about candidate eligibility; the earlier lack of candidate findings is retained above as history. ACT-A: owner accepted; control field-verified at the work location; no transfer to an unassessed work area. Qualifies. Residual risk: 8 points. ACT-B: owner accepted; control field-verified at the work location; no transfer to an unassessed work area. Qualifies. Residual risk: 3 points. ACT-C: owner accepted and no transfer to an unassessed work area, but control has not been field-verified. Nonqualifier because field verification is required, notwithstanding its lowest score of 1 point. ACT-D: owner accepted and field-verified, but transfers the hazard to an unassessed work area. Nonqualifier because hazard transfer is disqualifying; residual risk: 5 points.

Recomputed eligible set: ACT-B (3 risk points) and ACT-A (8 risk points), ordered lowest first; the eligible selection of exactly one item is ACT-B (3 risk points). Candidate findings and the stated conditions establish no additional qualification requirements. The safety director release status for SAFE-510 remains unknown/pending; this evidence does not establish release. No scheduling result is decided or inferred.

Request ID SAFE-510 is a workplace safety corrective-action review. The request is to select exactly one eligible item, if any qualify. A corrective action qualifies only when its hazard-control owner accepted the action, the control was field-verified, and the action does not transfer the hazard to an unassessed work area. Rank qualifying actions by residual risk points after correction, lowest first; ties use ascending complete action ID. Scheduling requires a safety director release. If no item qualifies, the decision is no_action; if the nonempty eligible selection has a safety director release recorded for request SAFE-510, the decision is schedule; otherwise, the decision is hold. The authority is scoped to request SAFE-510; no separate item-specific authorization is required.

Latest evidence: The measured candidate register for SAFE-510 records ACT-A at 8 risk points after correction, ACT-B at 3 risk points after correction, ACT-C at 1 risk point after correction, and ACT-D at 5 risk points after correction. Based only on these metrics, the provisional lowest-first worklist is ACT-C (1 risk point), ACT-B (3 risk points), ACT-D (5 risk points), ACT-A (8 risk points). This provisional ordering establishes neither eligibility nor authorization. The latest evidence provides no candidate-item findings establishing owner acceptance, field verification, or absence of hazard transfer; eligibility therefore remains unknown. The latest evidence records no safety director release status; release status therefore remains unknown. No decision is made.

Earlier-pass history: Earlier notes recorded no evidence reviewed for case UNKNOWN; that was superseded by the subsequently identified request SAFE-510. In the prior SAFE-510 pass, no candidate-item findings, residual-risk metric, or recorded safety director release status were available, so those remained unknown/pending then. The current status above is based on the latest measured candidate register, which now supplies metrics but not eligibility or release evidence.

Current evidence update (SAFE-510): The condition review supersedes the earlier uncertainty about candidate eligibility; the earlier lack of candidate findings is retained above as history. ACT-A: owner accepted; control field-verified at the work location; no transfer to an unassessed work area. Qualifies. Residual risk: 8 points. ACT-B: owner accepted; control field-verified at the work location; no transfer to an unassessed work area. Qualifies. Residual risk: 3 points. ACT-C: owner accepted and no transfer to an unassessed work area, but control has not been field-verified. Nonqualifier because field verification is required, notwithstanding its lowest score of 1 point. ACT-D: owner accepted and field-verified, but transfers the hazard to an unassessed work area. Nonqualifier because hazard transfer is disqualifying; residual risk: 5 points.

Recomputed eligible set: ACT-B (3 risk points) and ACT-A (8 risk points), ordered lowest first; the eligible selection of exactly one item is ACT-B (3 risk points). Candidate findings and the stated conditions establish no additional qualification requirements. The safety director release status for SAFE-510 remains unknown/pending; this evidence does not establish release. No scheduling result is decided or inferred.

sources.text: Safety assurance office opened workplace safety corrective-action review request SAFE-510. Schedule items for SAFE-510. Select exactly one eligible item if any qualify. Decision rule: A corrective action qualifies only when its hazard-control owner accepted the action, the control was field-verified, and the action does not transfer the hazard to an unassessed work area. Rank qualifying actions by residual risk points after correction, lowest first; ties use ascending complete action ID. Scheduling requires a safety director release. Selection cardinality: exactly one if any qualify; ascending residual risk points after correction; ties by ascending complete ID Decision mapping: if no item qualifies, use no_action; if the nonempty eligible selection has a safety director release for request SAFE-510 recorded, use schedule; otherwise use hold. The authority is scoped to request SAFE-510; do not add a separate item-specific authorization requirement.

sources.text:
Evidence condition review for SAFE-510:
ACT-A: Owner acceptance: the named hazard-control owner accepted this action. Field verification: the control was verified at the work location. Hazard transfer: no unassessed work area receives the hazard.
ACT-B: Owner acceptance: the named hazard-control owner accepted this action. Field verification: the control was verified at the work location. Hazard transfer: no unassessed work area receives the hazard.
ACT-C: Owner acceptance: the named hazard-control owner accepted this action. Field verification: the control has not been verified at the work location. Hazard transfer: no unassessed work area receives the hazard.
ACT-D: Owner acceptance: the named hazard-control owner accepted this action. Field verification: the control was verified at the work location. Hazard transfer: the action transfers the hazard to an unassessed work area.
A lower residual-risk score cannot replace owner acceptance or field verification.

Request SAFE-512: The Safety assurance office opened a workplace safety corrective-action review and requests scheduling items for this request. Select exactly one eligible action if any qualify. An action qualifies only if its hazard-control owner accepted it, its control was field-verified, and it does not transfer the hazard to an unassessed work area. Rank qualifying actions by residual risk points after correction, lowest first; break ties by ascending complete action ID. If no item qualifies, map the selection to no_action. If the nonempty eligible selection has a safety director release for request SAFE-512 recorded, map to schedule; otherwise map to hold. The authority prerequisite is a safety director release scoped to request SAFE-512; its observed status is unknown/pending. No candidate eligibility findings or metrics are provided, so candidate/item findings remain unknown/pending.

Current candidate-register pass: For SAFE-512, measured residual risk points after correction are ACT-J: 1 risk points; ACT-K: 2 risk points; ACT-L: 3 risk points; ACT-M: 4 risk points. Provisional metric-only ordering, lowest first: ACT-J, ACT-K, ACT-L, ACT-M. These metrics do not establish eligibility. Candidate eligibility findings (owner acceptance, field verification, and no transfer to an unassessed work area) remain unknown/pending. The safety director release scoped to request SAFE-512 remains unknown/pending; this file contains no release evidence. No final selection or decision is made.

Current conditions-and-exceptions pass for SAFE-512: ACT-J — owner accepted; control not field-verified; no transfer to an unassessed work area; ineligible because field verification is absent. ACT-L — owner accepted; control field-verified; transfers the hazard to an unassessed work area; ineligible because of that transfer. ACT-M — owner has not accepted; control not field-verified; no transfer to an unassessed work area; ineligible because owner acceptance and field verification are absent. Previously recorded residual risk points after correction remain ACT-J: 1 risk points; ACT-K: 2 risk points; ACT-L: 3 risk points; ACT-M: 4 risk points; these metrics do not establish eligibility. No candidate is currently eligible. The safety director release scoped to SAFE-512 remains unknown/pending; no release evidence is provided. No final selection or decision is made.

Candidate eligibility findings and metrics are unchanged: no candidate is eligible, and residual risk points after correction remain ACT-J: 1 risk points; ACT-K: 2 risk points; ACT-L: 3 risk points; ACT-M: 4 risk points. site.realized_instruction: Read only the supplied current-pass FileHandle, which is a read-only snapshot, and priorNotes. Maintain a complete running evidence record in readable prose, not a Draft-shaped JSON summary. Preserve every observed candidate eligibility finding, exact metric and unit, and the exact named authority prerequisite and its observed status. When later applicable evidence supersedes earlier uncertainty or a prior current-status statement, preserve that earlier statement only as explicitly labeled earlier-pass history, then append a clearly labeled current status tied to the latest evidence. The latest applicable observed evidence controls final interpretation. Do not leave conflicting current-status statements unresolved, but do not require global prose rewriting of the accumulated history. Carry supported facts forward; keep facts absent from current evidence and prior notes unknown or pending. An outstanding or next-step note is not evidence that a fact is present in the current file. Complete only this evidence pass. Do not collapse notes into selected IDs, measures, or a decision; the final interpreter makes the decision from the accumulated record. Keep historical events distinct from the requested decision. Do not invent facts. Keep historical events (what already happened) distinct from the requested decision (what must be decided now). Do not invent facts. Return the complete accumulated readable prose as the Neuralese<string> result to the caller. For computed text, build an ordinary string in eval and return that value directly. Marker bodies are literal text and do not interpolate JavaScript variables. This note child does not write files; the parent owns the final decision.json write.

Rank qualifying records by independent provenance links, greatest first; ties use ascending complete record ID. Reconciliation requires a records custodian approval. Selection cardinality: exactly one if any qualify; descending independent provenance links; ties by ascending complete ID Decision mapping: if no item qualifies, use no_action; if the nonempty eligible selection has a records custodian approval for request PROV-522 recorded, use reconcile; otherwise use hold. The authority is scoped to request PROV-522; do not add a separate item-specific authorization requirement. No item-specific evidence, eligibility finding, metric, or approval status is provided in this pass; these remain unknown. This is no evidence yet, not a negative finding. The earlier notes contained only a placeholder and add no reviewed evidence or decision. Candidate-register pass: recorded metrics for PROV-522 are REC-J: 8 verified links, REC-K: 6 verified links, REC-L: 5 verified links, and REC-M: 4 verified links (each metric is independent provenance links). Provisional ordering/worklist based only on these registered metrics, greatest first: REC-J, REC-K, REC-L, REC-M. Eligibility, exceptions, and authorization are unchecked/unknown, not negative. This ordering is provisional and is not a present decision; no decision fields are assigned.

REC-K: Original source: the original issuing source is not identified. Custody transfer: every transfer is documented in the custody log. Independent corroboration: an independent record confirms the key date.
REC-L: Original source: the original issuing source is identified. Custody transfer: every transfer is documented in the custody log. Independent corroboration: no independent record confirms the key date.
REC-M: Original source: the original issuing source is not identified. Custody transfer: a transfer is missing from the custody log. Independent corroboration: an independent record confirms the key date.
A high link count cannot establish an unknown original source or fill a custody gap.

Eligibility under the existing rule (identified original source AND documented custody transfer AND independent confirmation of the key date): REC-J is ineligible because a custody transfer is missing; REC-K is ineligible because its original source is not identified; REC-L is ineligible because no independent record confirms the key date; REC-M is ineligible because its original source is not identified and a transfer is missing. The high link count does not cure unknown source identification or a custody gap. Current eligible selected set: none. Current metric: none (no eligible item). The prior provisional metric order—REC-J, REC-K, REC-L, REC-M, based on 8, 6, 5, and 4 verified links respectively, each measured as independent provenance links—is history only, not the current result. template_segments: Read complete accumulated notes and decisionContext. Apply its explicit decision rule to supported facts. Historical events are evidence, not a substitute for deciding now. Do not require execution already occurred or add prerequisites absent from rule. Do not invent; follow uncertainty handling. Return exactly the declared Draft fields and formats.

block.body:
Evidence from pass “request scope and rule”: The request is EXPT-530, concerning selection and adoption of experimental protocol revisions for EXPT-530. A revision qualifies only if its primary outcome is preregistered, its control arm is retained, and its analysis plan handles the stated missing-data mechanism. Select up to two qualifying revisions with the fewest unresolved design deviations; break ties by ascending complete revision ID. Decision rule: if no item qualifies, use no_action. If the eligible selection is nonempty and principal investigator approval for request EXPT-530 is recorded, use adopt; otherwise use hold. Approval authority is scoped to request EXPT-530; no separate item-specific authorization requirement applies. This pass establishes the request scope and rule only; item eligibility, the selected items, and approval status remain unknown and pending.
Evidence from pass “candidate register”: The measured unresolved design deviations are REV-A: 6 deviations; REV-B: 3 deviations; REV-C: 1 deviations; REV-D: 4 deviations. Provisional metric-only worklist, ascending by deviations: REV-C (1 deviations), REV-B (3 deviations), REV-D (4 deviations), REV-A (6 deviations). This is not a final selection: eligibility has not yet been checked, and approval status for EXPT-530 remains unknown and pending.

Evidence from pass “conditions and exceptions”: For EXPT-530, eligibility requires all three stated conditions: a preregistered primary outcome, retained control arm, and an analysis plan addressing the observed missing-data mechanism. REV-A is eligible: its primary outcome was preregistered before enrollment, its control arm is retained, and its plan addresses the mechanism. REV-B is eligible for the same three reasons. REV-C is ineligible because its control arm is removed, despite preregistration and an adequate missing-data plan. REV-D is ineligible because its plan does not address the observed missing-data mechanism, despite preregistration and a retained control arm. The exception is explicit: fewer deviations do not cure any failed condition.

The prior metric-only worklist (REV-C, REV-B, REV-D, REV-A) is provisional and superseded for selection because it did not account for eligibility. The qualifying ranking, applying the preserved deviation counts and ascending-count rule, is REV-B (3 deviations), then REV-A (6 deviations). Selected up-to-two candidates: REV-B and REV-A. Principal investigator approval for request EXPT-530 remains pending/not recorded in the available evidence; therefore adoption is not established and the decision remains hold pending approval.

Evidence from pass “execution authority”: The action authority record for EXPT-530 states that principal investigator approval for EXPT-530 is signed. This later applicable evidence supersedes the earlier pending/not-recorded authority status: current status is approval recorded (signed) for request EXPT-530. The approval record is an authority event, distinct from the adoption decision. The eligible selection and measures remain REV-B (3 deviations), then REV-A (6 deviations); under the decision rule, the nonempty eligible selection with the required approval recorded supports adopt.

Select exactly one eligible item if any qualify. site.realized_instruction: Read only the supplied current-pass FileHandle, which is a read-only snapshot, and priorNotes. Maintain a complete running evidence record in readable prose, not a Draft-shaped JSON summary. Preserve every observed candidate eligibility finding, exact metric and unit, and the exact named authority prerequisite and its observed status. When later applicable evidence supersedes earlier uncertainty or a prior current-status statement, preserve that earlier statement only as explicitly labeled earlier-pass history, then append a clearly labeled current status tied to the latest evidence. The latest applicable observed evidence controls final interpretation. Do not leave conflicting current-status statements unresolved, but do not require global prose rewriting of the accumulated history. Carry supported facts forward; keep facts absent from current evidence and prior notes unknown or pending. An outstanding or next-step note is not evidence that a fact is present in the current file. Complete only this evidence pass. Do not collapse notes into selected IDs, measures, or a decision; the final interpreter makes the decision from the accumulated record. Keep historical events distinct from the requested decision. Do not invent facts. Keep historical events (what already happened) distinct from the requested decision (what must be decided now). Do not invent facts. Return the complete accumulated readable prose as the Neuralese<string> result to the caller. For computed text, build an ordinary string in eval and return that value directly. Marker bodies are literal text and do not interpolate JavaScript variables. This note child does not write files; the parent owns the final decision.json write.

REQUEST SCOPE AND RULE — current evidence (pass-01-request.md): The Study design review group opened experimental protocol revision selection request EXPT-531; the request says to adopt items for EXPT-531. Select exactly one eligible item if any qualify. A protocol revision qualifies only when its primary outcome is preregistered, its control arm is retained, and its analysis plan handles the stated missing-data mechanism. Among qualifying revisions, select the one with the fewest unresolved design deviations; ties are resolved by ascending complete revision ID. Adoption requires principal investigator approval. If no item qualifies, decision is no_action. If the nonempty eligible selection has the principal investigator approval for request EXPT-531 recorded, decision is adopt; otherwise decision is hold. The authority is scoped to request EXPT-531; no separate item-specific authorization requirement applies. No candidate eligibility findings, deviation metrics, or observed approval status are present in this pass. Earlier placeholder history: prior notes stated that case UNKNOWN had no evidence reviewed; this is superseded for current request identification by EXPT-531 above. Candidate findings and approval status remain unknown pending applicable evidence.

CURRENT EVIDENCE PASS — candidate register (pass-02-register.md): The measured candidate register for EXPT-531 reports REV-E: 2 unresolved design deviations; REV-F: 2 unresolved design deviations; REV-G: 1 unresolved design deviation; REV-H: 5 unresolved design deviations. Metric-only provisional ordering: REV-G (1), REV-E and REV-F tied (2 each; ascending complete ID would place REV-E before REV-F if otherwise eligible), then REV-H (5). These counts do not establish qualification or approval. Current candidate eligibility status: unknown for REV-E, REV-F, REV-G, and REV-H pending the required primary-outcome preregistration, retained-control-arm, and missing-data-analysis findings. Current principal investigator approval status for request EXPT-531: unknown; this register does not report it. The EXPT-531 selection and adoption rules remain as stated above; this is metric evidence, not a final selection or decision.

REV-H: Outcome preregistration: the primary outcome is preregistered before enrollment. Control arm: the planned control arm is retained. Missing-data plan: the analysis plan addresses the observed missing-data mechanism.

Decision rule: A protocol revision qualifies only when its primary outcome is preregistered, its control arm is retained, and its analysis plan handles the stated missing-data mechanism. Select up to two qualifying revisions with the fewest unresolved design deviations, ties by ascending complete revision ID. Adoption requires principal investigator approval. Selection cardinality: up to 2; ascending unresolved design deviations; ties by ascending complete ID Decision mapping: if no item qualifies, use no_action; if the nonempty eligible selection has the principal investigator approval for request EXPT-532 recorded, use adopt; otherwise use hold. The authority is scoped to request EXPT-532; do not add a separate item-specific authorization requirement.

sources.text:
Evidence condition review for EXPT-532:
REV-J: Outcome preregistration: the primary outcome is preregistered before enrollment. Control arm: the planned control arm is removed. Missing-data plan: the analysis plan addresses the observed missing-data mechanism.
REV-K: Outcome preregistration: the primary outcome was not preregistered before enrollment. Control arm: the planned control arm is retained. Missing-data plan: the analysis plan addresses the observed missing-data mechanism.
REV-L: Outcome preregistration: the primary outcome is preregistered before enrollment. Control arm: the planned control arm is retained. Missing-data plan: the analysis plan does not address the observed missing-data mechanism.
REV-M: Outcome preregistration: the primary outcome is preregistered before enrollment. Control arm: the planned control arm is retained. Missing-data plan: the analysis plan addresses the observed missing-data mechanism.
Fewer deviations do not cure a missing preregistration, removed control arm, or unhandled missing-data mechanism.

A window qualifies only when the required skill is staffed, the resource is available for the full interval, and the assignment respects the worker rest rule. Select the qualifying windows with the earliest completion time; break ties by ascending complete window ID. Selection is ranked by completion time in minutes, with ties by ascending complete ID. If no item qualifies, the decision is no_action. If the nonempty eligible selection has an operations lead release recorded for request SCHED-540, the decision is assign; otherwise, it is hold. Assignment requires an operations lead release. Authority is scoped to request SCHED-540; do not add a separate item-specific authorization requirement.

Operations scheduling desk opened constrained resource-window scheduling request SCHED-540. Assign items for SCHED-540, selecting up to two eligible work windows. A window qualifies only when the required skill is staffed, the resource is available for the full interval, and the assignment respects the worker rest rule. Select the qualifying windows with the earliest completion time; break ties by ascending complete window ID. Selection is ranked by completion time in minutes, with ties by ascending complete ID. If no item qualifies, the decision is no_action. If the nonempty eligible selection has an operations lead release recorded for request SCHED-540, the decision is assign; otherwise, it is hold. Assignment requires an operations lead release. Authority is scoped to request SCHED-540; do not add a separate item-specific authorization requirement.

Historical provisional ranking by measured completion time (ascending; ties by ascending complete ID): WIN-C — 65 minutes; WIN-D — 75 minutes; WIN-B — 80 minutes; WIN-A — 95 minutes. This ranking was based only on supplied measured candidate times and is superseded for selection by the eligibility review below.

For SCHED-540, WIN-A satisfies skill coverage, full-interval resource availability, and rest compliance; WIN-B also satisfies all three conditions. WIN-C fails eligibility because the resource is unavailable during part of the interval, despite skill coverage and rest compliance. WIN-D fails eligibility because the worker does not meet the required rest interval, despite skill coverage and full-interval resource availability. Earlier completion cannot waive these conditions. The eligible set is WIN-B and WIN-A; ranked by earliest completion time, the selected items are WIN-B; WIN-A. Their completion times, in ranked order, are 80; 95 minutes. Assignment is not decided; operations lead release status for SCHED-540 remains unknown.

Evidence condition review for SCHED-540:
WIN-A: Skill coverage: a currently qualified worker covers the required skill. Resource availability: the resource is available for the complete interval. Rest compliance: the worker meets the required rest interval.
WIN-B: Skill coverage: a currently qualified worker covers the required skill. Resource availability: the resource is available for the complete interval. Rest compliance: the worker meets the required rest interval.
WIN-C: Skill coverage: a currently qualified worker covers the required skill. Resource availability: the resource is unavailable during part of the interval. Rest compliance: the worker meets the required rest interval.

An earlier completion time cannot waive skill coverage, full-interval availability, or worker rest.

block.body: Request-scope and rule history (current pass: request scope and rule): The constrained resource-window scheduling request is SCHED-541, and items are assigned for SCHED-541. Select exactly one eligible item if any qualify. A work window qualifies only when the required skill is staffed, the resource is available for the full interval, and the assignment respects the worker rest rule. Among qualifying windows, select exactly one with the earliest completion time; ties are broken by ascending complete window ID. Selection cardinality is exactly one if any qualify, ordered by ascending completion time in minutes with ties by ascending complete ID. Assignment requires an operations lead release. If no item qualifies, the decision is no_action. If the nonempty eligible selection has an operations lead release recorded for request SCHED-541, the decision is assign; otherwise it is hold. The authority is scoped to request SCHED-541; no separate item-specific authorization requirement applies. This pass supplies no candidate findings, metrics, or release status.

Select exactly one eligible item if any qualify. Request-scope and rule history (current pass: request scope and rule): The constrained resource-window scheduling request is SCHED-541, and items are assigned for SCHED-541. Select exactly one eligible item if any qualify. The final route advice emphasizes: identify candidates only from the explicit findings, compute each item's elapsed completion time from the stated start and duration, and test that entire work window against staffing, resource availability, and rest. Return every qualifying item with exact supporting source phrases and arithmetic; do not apply earliest-completion selection until a later pass directs it. Latest status: metrics recorded and ordered; qualification and release remain unchecked; no decision is made.

WIN-J: Skill coverage: a currently qualified worker covers the required skill. Resource availability: the resource is unavailable during part of the interval. Rest compliance: the worker meets the required rest interval.

WIN-L: Skill coverage: a currently qualified worker covers the required skill. Resource availability: the resource is available for the complete interval. Rest compliance: the worker does not meet the required rest interval.
